newsitem.title: USA: Gilead does not see profit for FY 97.
newsitem.headline: Gilead does not see profit for FY 97.

text.p: Gilead Sciences Inc said Thursday it does not expect to achieve profitability in the remaining quarters of the year or for the full year 1997.
Earlier, Gilead reported second quarter earnings of $2,711,000 or $0.09 per share, compared to a net loss of $12,158,000 or $0.43 per share for the same quarter in 1996.

The company said its profitability for the second quarter 1997 was primarily the result of milestone payments recognized from collaborations with Pharmacia & Upjohn S.A. and with F. Hoffmann-La Roche.

Gilead received a $10 million milestone payment from Pharmacia & Upjohn after VISTIDE, its anti-viral treatment for AIDS-related blindness, was authorized for marketing in the European Union. Pharmacia & Upjohn has exclusive rights to market VISTIDE outside the United States.

Gilead also received a $3 million milestone payment from La Roche for a collaboration to develop compounds for treating and preventing viral influenza. Gilead and Roche are now testing GS 4104 in Phase II human studies in the U.S.
"Those are one-time events, and therefore will impact just this quarter," said Gilead spokeswoman Lana Lauher.
